content:
With early voting underway in Texas and Election Day set for Tuesday, November 3, the top federal prosecutor for South Texas is putting anyone who would break federal election law on notice.

U.S. Attorney Aaron Reitz, whose Southern District of Texas covers Houston, the Gulf Coast, and the Rio Grande Valley — about 10 million people, including Laredo and Webb County — issued a video statement on Oct. 19 announcing three election-integrity steps his office is taking, according to the U.S. Department of Justice.

First, Reitz said he has appointed both civil and criminal District Election Officers. Working with the Justice Department's Civil Rights Division, these attorneys will assist and advise teams of election monitors at key polling locations to oversee compliance with federal law. Reitz stressed they are not armed agents but lawyers, noting the Justice Department has done this work for decades.

Second, his office has established standard operating procedures with the Texas Secretary of State and the Texas Attorney General to take up and investigate credible referrals alleging violations of federal law.

Third, Reitz said he has coordinated with the Department of Homeland Security, the FBI, and the Civil Rights Division to surge legal resources where they are needed most.

Reitz emphasized that state and local officials have primary responsibility for administering elections under the U.S. Constitution, and that complaints about election administration should go to them first. His role, he said, is different: as the senior federal law-enforcement officer for the district, he stands as a backstop to ensure federal law is upheld.

"It means that only eligible voters can vote — no barred felons, no aliens, and no foreigners. American elections are for Americans only," Reitz said. "It means no foreign influence on our election infrastructure, in campaign finance, or at the ballot box." He added that there is "no crooked local election administrators" tolerance — administrators have a duty to prevent illegal voting — and "no fraud," calling accurate voter rolls, honest paperwork, secure ballots, and lawful procedures essential.

"So let me be clear: If you violate federal election law, I will hunt you down and prosecute you," Reitz said. "Election Day is Tuesday, November 3rd. We'll see you out at the polls."

Sources: U.S. Department of Justice, U.S. Attorney's Office for the Southern District of Texas, Oct. 19, 2026.

Webb Watch 956
excerpt: U.S. Attorney Aaron Reitz announced Oct. 19 that his office is appointing election officers, coordinating with Texas officials, and surging FBI and DHS legal resources to enforce federal election law through the Nov. 3 election.
title: U.S. Attorney Reitz deploys federal election monitors, investigators for South Texas elections
